content.value_statement: Teams need repeatable source code security checks before release. This skill helps configure SAST tools, triage findings, and map fixes to secure coding patterns.
actual_capabilities: Selects SAST tools for Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, Ruby, PHP, Go, and Rust projects.
Provides Bandit, Semgrep, ESLint Security, Brakeman, gosec, SpotBugs, PMD, CodeQL, and clippy scan guidance.
Explains detection patterns for SQL injection, XSS, hardcoded secrets, path traversal, command injection, and unsafe deserialization.
Shows framework checks for Django, Flask, Express, Spring Boot, Rails, Laravel, and React security issues.
Includes Semgrep rule examples for custom security policies.
Provides CI examples for GitHub Actions and GitLab security scan workflows.
limitations: It requires source code or build outputs to perform useful analysis.
It does not replace runtime testing, penetration testing, or manual exploit validation.
External tools must be installed or available in the target environment.
Rules can produce false positives and need project-specific tuning.

use_cases.title: Pull Request Security Review
use_cases.description: Run targeted SAST checks on changed files and prioritize exploitable findings before merge.

use_cases.title: CI Security Gate Setup
use_cases.description: Add repeatable Bandit, Semgrep, or ESLint Security scans to a build pipeline with clear report outputs.

use_cases.title: Legacy Code Baseline
use_cases.description: Assess an older codebase, group findings by severity, and plan incremental remediation work.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic SAST Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner scan of a small repository
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the SAST skill to review this repository. Identify languages, choose suitable tools, and summarize the highest-risk vulnerability patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Triage Scanner Findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the SAST skill to triage these scanner findings. Group confirmed risks, likely false positives, and fixes by severity.

prompt_templates.title: Create CI SAST Checks
prompt_templates.scenario: Add scanning to a release workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the SAST skill to design a CI security scan for this project. Recommend tools, thresholds, artifacts, and developer feedback steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design Custom Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the SAST skill to draft custom Semgrep rules for our secure coding policy. Explain the target pattern, expected matches, and test cases.

output_examples.input: Review a Python Flask service for common SAST issues.
output_examples.output: The review highlights debug mode, weak secret key handling, unsafe file access, and missing secure headers. It recommends Bandit and Semgrep checks with prioritized fixes.

output_examples.input: Add SAST scanning to a pull request workflow.
output_examples.output: The plan runs lightweight scans on pull requests, stores reports as artifacts, and blocks only confirmed high-severity findings after triage.

output_examples.input: Triage a mixed Semgrep and Bandit report.
output: Confirmed injection findings are listed first.
Likely false positives are separated with rationale.
Each fix is mapped to an owner and severity.

best_practices: Run SAST early in development and again in CI before release.
Tune rules and exclusions so developers trust the findings.
Prioritize confirmed critical and high findings before broad cleanup work.
anti_patterns: Do not upload proprietary code to external services without approval.
Do not block releases on untriaged low-confidence findings.
Do not rely on one scanner as the only security review method.

faq.question: Does this skill run scanners automatically?
faq.answer: It provides guidance and commands for SAST workflows. Tool execution depends on the user environment and approval process.

faq.question: Which languages does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, Ruby, PHP, Go, Rust, and related framework patterns.

faq.question: Can it replace penetration testing?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on static source review and should be combined with runtime testing for stronger assurance.

faq.question: Can it help with custom policies?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Semgrep rule guidance for organization-specific security checks.

faq.question: How should teams handle false positives?
faq.answer: Teams should tune rules, document accepted risk, and keep confirmed findings separate from noisy results.

faq.question: Does it cover compliance mapping?
faq.answer: It references OWASP, PCI-DSS, and SOC 2 contexts, but compliance evidence still needs human review.
